# Daag: Online Gender Violence Archive, Bangladesh

> Before you trust someone, see what they wrote. A verified public record of abusive and victim-blaming comments on gender violence in Bangladesh.

> Source: https://www.daag-bd.com/

## Behind the polite face, read what he wrote.

One comment on its own might mean nothing. A few of them side by side, and you know the man.

One incident, step by step

### One news story. Four hundred comments. Three are kept.

Easier to show than to tell. Tap through the steps.

- 01 
 The story breaks 
 A woman has been attacked. The press reports it. The post is public. Anyone can read it.

- 02 
 The comments fill up 
 Four hundred within hours. Most are sympathetic. Some are not: blame, abuse, threats.

- 03 
 Someone notices 
 Anyone can send the link and a screenshot without giving their name. It takes two minutes.

- 04 
 A person checks it 
 The link is opened and matched by hand, the screenshot checked for edits. Most submissions are rejected right here.

- 05 
 Three are kept 
 The post may be deleted later. The account may change. But what was written stays on record.

Try to erase it

### Deleting it does not erase it.

Hold the mouse down and rub the line out. However hard you rub, the mark stays. The internet works the same way.

মেয়েটা অত রাতে বাইরে কী করছিল, সেটা আগে জিজ্ঞেস করুন।

#### Check someone. Don’t hunt them.

Everyone has a right to know who they are dealing with. Daag exists for exactly that: one look before you trust someone, hire them, or marry into their family.

But that is where it ends. Do not take these records and brigade someone, circulate their address or phone number, or threaten them. Any such complaint, once proven, means the account is removed.

We hold only comments that were published in the open. Phone numbers, home addresses, private profiles and anything from a closed group never enter this archive.

Anyone who believes a record in their name is wrong can dispute it. The moderator who approved it does not handle the dispute. A different one reviews it within 14 working days.

Emergency helpline

### In danger now? Call. Don’t wait.

Daag keeps records; it cannot come and get you. If someone is threatening you, blackmailing you, or has raised a hand to you, call one of the numbers below without delay. All of them are open day and night, and the calls are free.
